meta.title: 3D bioprinting patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell models of Alzheimer's disease using a smart bioink.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Healthy and Alzheimer's patient-derived hiPSC neural progenitors were bioprinted in a fibrin-based bioink on the Aspect RX1 microfluidic printer, with or without drug-releasing PCL microspheres. Constructs stayed viable for 30-45 days and were characterized for viability, markers and calcium signalling.

formulations.crosslinking: CaCl2 + chitosan + thrombin crosslinker, co-extruded in microfluidic printhead
formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 90 mbar (bioink channel); crosslinker 100 mbar, buffer 500 mbar.
formulations.name: Fibrin bioink (AD, no microspheres)
formulations.composition_detail: 20 mg/mL fibrinogen, 0.5% w/v alginate, 0.3 mg/mL genipin
formulations.cell_type: neural progenitor cells (basal forebrain cholinergic neuron differentiation)
formulations.key_outcome: Viability 83.8% on day 1 and 78.8% on day 30 for AD constructs without microspheres.

evidence.quote: fibrinogen (cat no. 341578, EMD Millipore, Burlington, MA, USA) was prepared at a concentration of 20 mg/mL, 0.5% w/v sodium alginate
mixed with the primed neural progenitor cells (NPCs) at a concentration of 1 × 106 cells/mL of bioink
The pressures were set at 100 mbar, 90 mbar, and 500 mbar for the crosslinker, bioink, and buffer, respectively.
A printing speed of 25 mm/s and a 40% rectilinear infill pattern were used
On day 1 directly after bioprinting, cell viability for the AD C group was 83.78 ± 4.96%

formulations.crosslinking: CaCl2 + chitosan + thrombin crosslinker, co-extruded in microfluidic printhead
formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 90 mbar. The large day-30 drop vs. the no-microsphere group is worth discussing with the authors.
formulations.name: Fibrin bioink + purmorphamine PCL microspheres (AD)
formulations.composition_detail: 20 mg/mL fibrinogen, 0.5% w/v alginate, 0.3 mg/mL genipin; PCL microspheres 1 mg/mL
formulations.cell_type: neural progenitor cells (basal forebrain cholinergic neuron differentiation)
formulations.key_outcome: Microspheres raised day-1 viability to 92.2%, but viability fell to 43.9% by day 30.

evidence.quote: The bioink including cells and PCL microspheres encapsulated with puro were used to print tissue constructs.
The pressures were set at 100 mbar, 90 mbar, and 500 mbar for the crosslinker, bioink, and buffer, respectively.
A printing speed of 25 mm/s and a 40% rectilinear infill pattern were used
AD CM had a viability of 92.16 ± 5.94%
the AD CM group with a viability of 43.92 ± 12.52%
